You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 96be65d12d792b3e177505db1225e1ec4f9cf5cd Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Wei Yongjun <weiyongjun1@huawei.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Feb 2019 09:18:41 +0000
Subject: [PATCH] gpio: tqmx86: Drop unnecessary gpiochip_remove in
 tqmx86_gpio_probe()

It's not necessary to remove gpio_chip which added with
devm_gpiochip_add_data().

Fixes: b868db94a6a7 ("gpio: tqmx86: Add GPIO from for this IO controller")
Signed-off-by: Wei Yongjun <weiyongjun1@huawei.com>
Reviewed-by: Andrew Lunn <andrew@lunn.ch>
Signed-off-by: Linus Walleij <linus.walleij@linaro.org>
---
 drivers/gpio/gpio-tqmx86.c | 4 +---
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 3 deletions(-)

diff --git a/drivers/gpio/gpio-tqmx86.c b/drivers/gpio/gpio-tqmx86.c
index 6f7250c6f597..33dbe483f92f 100644
--- a/drivers/gpio/gpio-tqmx86.c
+++ b/drivers/gpio/gpio-tqmx86.c
@@ -291,7 +291,7 @@ static int tqmx86_gpio_probe(struct platform_device *pdev)
 					   IRQ_TYPE_EDGE_BOTH);
 		if (ret) {
 			dev_err(dev, "Could not add irq chip\n");
-			goto out_remove;
+			goto out_pm_dis;
 		}
 
 		gpiochip_set_chained_irqchip(chip, irq_chip,
@@ -309,8 +309,6 @@ static int tqmx86_gpio_probe(struct platform_device *pdev)
 
 	return 0;
 
-out_remove:
-	gpiochip_remove(&gpio->chip);
 out_pm_dis:
 	pm_runtime_disable(&pdev->dev);
 
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by an unnecessary call to `gpiochip_remove` in the `tqmx86_gpio_probe` function. The `gpiochip_remove` function was being invoked even when the GPIO chip was added using `devm_gpiochip_add_data`, which automatically manages the lifecycle of the GPIO chip and removes it when the device is removed. This led to an incorrect attempt to remove a GPIO chip that was already managed by the device management framework, potentially causing resource management issues or crashes. The patch corrects this by removing the unnecessary call to `gpiochip_remove`.

You are a programming expert.
    You will be given the root cause of a bug and  the corresponding patch.
    You need to extract the code statements that lead to the bug from  the patch, based on the root cause.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by an unnecessary call to `gpiochip_remove` in the `tqmx86_gpio_probe` function. The `gpiochip_remove` function was being invoked even when the GPIO chip was added using `devm_gpiochip_add_data`, which automatically manages the lifecycle of the GPIO chip and removes it when the device is removed. This led to an incorrect attempt to remove a GPIO chip that was already managed by the device management framework, potentially causing resource management issues or crashes. The patch corrects this by removing the unnecessary call to `gpiochip_remove`.
